title: Shadow traffic shards + phased LTS upgrade workflow with adaptive rollback
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Design and implement a phased LTS upgrade workflow that uses traffic shards and a 'shadow canary' mode to validate runtime changes without exposing new behavior to production users. The goal is to reduce blast radius for major LTS promotions and provide deterministic, observable gates for automated percent ramps and rollback.

Background: Current staged rollouts rely on simple % ramps and canaries tied to a small subset of users. For major LTS upgrades (model runtime and kernel changes) we need: (1) deterministic telemetry from new code under production load but without serving user-visible outputs, (2) stronger multi-signal gates (latency P99, tail CPU/memory, error spike, and quality regressions measured via eval proxies), and (3) safe automatic rollback with an investigation handoff.

Scope and features:
- Traffic shards: partition traffic by a deterministic shard key so we can route exact fractions of requests to runtime-vN while keeping customer affinity preserved. Shards can be assigned to passive (shadow), active (live), or withheld states.
- Shadow canary: duplicate traffic to a new version in shadow mode where responses are not returned to users but are processed end-to-end for telemetry and quality evaluation (including streaming path). This captures KV cache warming, batching behavior, and sequence-length effects.
- Phased ramps: support staged ramp plans (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with automated hold conditions and adaptive step-back when gate thresholds breach. Ramps are configurable per-release and per-route.
- Multi-signal gates: pipeline evaluates: 1) service-level metrics (5xx rate, 4xx anomalies), 2) performance (p99 latency, token throughput), 3) resource signals (GPU memory pressure, queue length), 4) quality proxies (synthetic prompt evals / reranking delta) and 5) customer-error-surface (logged unhappy sessions). All gates are weighted; combined score triggers hold or rollback.
- Auto-rollback and investigation: when combined score breaches the safety window, the system will either pause the ramp and alert SRE/RE or automatically roll back to previous runtime. Rollback includes a post-mortem stub with captured telemetry and a pointer to the failed shard IDs.
- Integration with feature flags and customer pins: enable per-customer opt-in/out via flags, and allow LTS pinning to force a specific version for enterprise customers.
- Orchestration CLI + Console UX: CLI to run dry-runs and aborts; Console will show per-shard health, timeline of ramps, and quality deltas.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Shadow duplication increases cost (double work for shadowed requests). We limit shadowing to small shards and schedule shadow runs during low-cost windows for expensive models.
- Shadow vs canary: shadow canaries avoid exposing user-visible regressions but may miss user-interaction downstream effects (e.g., webhooks). We'll pair shadowing with a small active canary cohort for end-to-end path coverage.
- Gate complexity: multi-signal gates reduce false positives but add configuration surface. Default conservative thresholds will be provided; power users can tune.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement traffic sharding controller and API that can create shards and assign state (shadow/active/withheld).
- Shadow duplication pipeline that records full trace and stores outputs in a quality evaluation bucket without returning them to users.
- Ramp policy engine supporting scheduled ramps, hold conditions, rollback rules, and manual overrides.
- Console views for shard health and an automatic incident link on rollbacks.
- End-to-end test demonstrating a staged upgrade where shadow telemetry detects a regression and prevents an active ramp.

Non-goals: automatic schema migrations for customer data, long-term storage of shadow outputs beyond 30 days, and per-request A/B experiments unrelated to safety gating.

Open questions:
- How much shadow traffic is affordable for large customers? (follow-up with finance to model cost).
- Which quality proxies are sufficient for automated gating vs those assigned to human review?

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1 (2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-16): prototyping traffic-shard controller and telemetry hooks (spike).
- Week 2 (2026-03-17 -> 2026-03-23): shadow duplication pipeline + basic quality-eval harness.
- Week 3 (2026-03-24 -> 2026-03-30): ramp policy engine + Console integration and runbook.
- Soft launch targeted at 2026-04-01 for internal teams and 2026-04-15 for limited external pilots.
